## Timing

The plan below adds up to about 75 minutes, which leaves about 15 minutes for questions in a 90-minute session.

| Part | Topic | Time (incl. TRY IT) | Start by |
|------|-------|---------------------|----------|
| 1 | R basics (1 TRY IT) | 10 min | 0:00 |
| 2 | Packages; error, warning, or message? | 10 min | 0:10 |
| 3 | Project folders and `here()` | 7 min | 0:20 |
| 4 | Importing data (1 TRY IT) | 8 min | 0:27 |
| 5 | Inspecting data (3 TRY ITs) | 25 min | 0:35 |
| 6 | The problem list (class + start TRY IT 6) | 10 min | 1:00 |
|   | Wrap-up and preview | 5 min | 1:10 |
|   | **Total** | **75 min** | |

**Running behind? Skip in this order:**

1.  TRY IT 6 (the measles problem list): start it, then assign the rest as homework. Learners need it at the start of Session 2.
2.  The ⭐ part of TRY IT 4 (`table()`).
3.  The 🧩 "Reading a function call" box in Part 4: point to it on screen 2 and move on.

**Never speed-run.** If you reach the end of the time, stop at the end of a part and point learners to the rest of the lesson page. Everything they need is there.

## Why this order

The session starts with the **basics of the language** (objects and functions), then the tools learners will use every day: packages, the project folder, importing, and inspecting. Session 1 calls one function at a time. The **pipe** `%>%`, `filter()`, and `arrange()` are taught at the start of Session 2. Building data frames by hand is in Session 4, and missing values and duplicates are in Session 3.

## Before you start

-   Check that everyone ran the [Setup](../setup.qmd) test. Anyone who didn't should start `install.packages()` **at the very beginning** of class — it can take several minutes, and Part 1 (R basics) needs no packages, so they can follow along while it installs. Windows users may need Rtools and Mac users may need the Xcode Command Line Tools ([Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.qmd)).
-   Hand out the green and red sticky notes and explain them.
-   Set up the questions **parking lot** (see the [Instructor Guide](index.qmd#teaching-with-two-instructors)).

## Teaching notes by part

**Part 1 — R basics.** Keep this brisk (about 10 minutes); learners practise all of it in every later session. Have someone make a deliberate mistake (`Mean(ages)`) to show that R is case-sensitive. The data frame diagram is **reading only**: point to it on screen 2 and explain "each column is one type". Nobody types `data.frame()` today.

**Part 2 — Packages, and error, warning, or message.** Show both ways to install: one package, `install.packages("janitor")`, and several at once with `c()` (the `c()` from Part 1). Nobody needs to run either if they did the setup: they only need the `library()` lines. Use the red text that `library(tidyverse)` just printed to introduce the table: "this red text is a message, nothing to do". Point out the "Asking for help" box: it's how you want questions phrased during the course.

**Part 3 — Project folders and `here()`.** Show that `here::here()` points at the workshop folder because it's open in Positron (and has a `.here` file). There is no TRY IT here; learners use `here()` in the import TRY IT next.

**Positron vs RStudio names:** if learners follow older tutorials, Positron's **Variables** pane is RStudio's **Environment** pane, and the **Explorer** is the **Files** pane.

**Part 5 — Inspecting.** This is the longest part. Start by reading the five questions at the top of Part 5 aloud: everything after answers one of them. The "Think about it" questions on the lesson page are prompts to ask the class:

-   *What is wrong with these column names?* — spaces, dots, capitals, mixed styles.
-   *Which column types look wrong?* — `date.onset` is text, `age` is text, and `age_unit` hints that some ages aren't in years.

After `skim()`, point at the `n_missing` column, the negative minimum of `wt_kg`, and the near-300 cm maximum of `ht_cm`. The 🔁 `table()` box and "Other ways to look" (`view()`, `names()`, `head()`) are **reading only**: mention them in one sentence each.

**TRY IT 5 — fix the broken code.** Give learners the time to struggle a little, then go through the four lines together and read each message aloud. The point of line 4 is that a warning can reveal a **data** problem rather than a typo.

**Part 6 — The problem list.** Build the list **with the class**: ask learners to call out what they found before showing the table. The "Fixed in" column previews Session 2. Duplicates are on the list as "not checked yet": Session 3 checks them.

## TRY IT answers at a glance

The numbers match the TRY IT numbers in the lesson, the student script, and the solutions file. Follow-along prompts are numbered by part (Follow along 5.3 = Part 5, third prompt).

| TRY IT | Answer |
|---|---|
| 1. Objects and functions | `mean(my_temps)` is 38.5 |
| 2. Import | `import(here("raw_data", "measles_raw.csv"))`: 1215 rows, 11 columns |
| 3. Size, structure, and summary | `Age (years)` is text; six names need backticks; the largest `Temp (C)` is 105 (104.7, a Fahrenheit value); 37 missing Patient IDs |
| 4. Categories | District has 18 values; "North" and "No" are each written 4 ways. ⭐ `table()` drops the 34 `NA` districts |
| 5. Fix the broken code | `count()` not `Count()`; `District` not `district`; `.csv` not `.cvs`; the warning from `mean()` is a data problem (`Age (years)` is text) |
| 6. Problem list | At least 8 problems — see the lesson's solution |
